reasons: Procedural defect (ordering / fresh-data precondition): DECL-C3-NT requires the crop picker to run before any render or map of the crop exists. A C2-NT-recipe map (base step-075000, no TTA, both orders) of the full w040 team SV canvas, which contains the whole NT crop, existed from 2026-09-24T23:33:18Z / 23:58:26Z (gpu_ledger row 37), about 1.5 h before the picker ran (2026-09-25T01:06:42Z) and before DECL-C3-NT was written (01:06:18Z). Its whole-canvas in-mask AUC (0.99659 / 0.49633; this crop is 17.1 % of those supervision pixels) was recorded in C3-RUN1 before the no-TTA variant was chosen, and the DECL-C3-NT disclosure names only the two excluded crops. On this crop that map already gives forward 0.99929 / reverse 0.54503 in the mask, so the gate outcome was contained in pre-existing data. The runner note "picker run once, before any render or map of the crop existed" is therefore not correct.

Everything else checks out: hashes match METRIC-HASH-8/7/0; crop re-derived (y0 512, x0 5376, 278,595 supervision px), no overlap with either earlier crop; label and supervision crops equal the Z = 14 source slices; no TTA in the inference log; w040_nt.tif = forward and w040_nt_reverse.tif = reverse per villa infer.py; all numbers re-derived with difference 0.0.
Bar outcomes on the re-derived numbers (recorded, not a verdict): pooled Pearson 0.9999993 MET (>= 0.999); forward AUC 0.99926 MET (>= 0.987); reverse AUC 0.56528 MET (< 0.60).

For the decision-maker: if the clause is read narrowly as "no render or map by OUR chain of OUR render of the crop", the within-run order holds and the procedure would be sound; the auditor reads "any ... map of it" literally, and the pre-existing map is the gated recipe on near-identical input, so the crop was not fresh for C2-NT.
